scope: Owner maintenance and private definition publication on macOS using synthetic CVDs and controlled I/O failures.
checks: Initial publication writes the reference and empty history atomically. An unchanged update preserves the reference.
A complete candidate stranded before the reference switch stays outside publication history even when its version is lower than the later active version and its detached evidence remains on disk.
Failures after replacing the reference report uncertainty. The reference that survives contains the current generation and its full predecessor history together.

Protection follows publication order and compares all CVD bytes and all three version numbers. Body corruption, version mismatch and a copy of the current content cannot serve as the protected predecessor.

A confirmed mismatch permits checking older published generations. Missing history, no intact predecessor, a timeout, a short read or an I/O error prevent generation deletion. A change after taking the selected lease leaves the selected directory, sidecar and lease intact.

The legacy reference is readable by scans and stays in place on unchanged updates. The first changed publication, including a change at the same version, records the former current generation and keeps other existing generation IDs protected as legacy untracked.

Current, last verified and leased generations stay protected. Selected deletion removes only the chosen entry and preserves the stored wait. A failed history rewrite leaves the record for a later verified cleanup behind an intact predecessor.

follow_up_2026_11_19.record_correction: this record names bcf0510 as its base and 804 tests, which matches the run before the change was committed; dd3c0d2 was committed on 87ec576, which adds 1 test, and its full suites on Python 3.14.10 and 3.15.2 gave 805 total, 788 passed, 17 skipped

findings.summary: after migration, every generation recorded as legacy_untracked stayed undeletable, so a store that kept 2 earlier generations reached the 4 slot limit with the first recorded publication and every later update stopped on capacity with nothing the CLI could delete; with 1 earlier generation it permanently took 1 of the 4 slots
findings.reproduced: with fake engines: 0.11.2 published versions 100, 101 and 102; dd3c0d2 then published 103, after which the listing showed the current generation, the protected predecessor and 2 legacy_untracked rows, none deletable, and the update to 104 ended with the capacity error. Under 0.11.2 the 2 older generations were deletable
findings.fix: once previous_protection is protected, legacy_untracked generations are deletable, and a deletion also removes the ID from legacy_untracked; while no intact recorded predecessor is confirmed they stay held. They predate the recorded former current generation or were never published, so they cannot be the latest published predecessor

findings.summary: a store that 0.11.2 had filled to 4 generations, which happens right after its fourth publication, could not migrate: the update stopped on capacity and every non-current generation was listed as legacy_history and could not be deleted
findings.reproduced: with fake engines: 0.11.2 published versions 100 to 103; dd3c0d2 ended the update to 104 with the capacity error and listed the 3 earlier generations as legacy_history, none deletable. Under 0.11.2 all 3 were deletable
findings.decision: option A chosen by the owner: until the first publication that records history, use the earlier release's rule
findings.fix: with the earlier reference format, a generation with valid headers and sizes, no version newer than the current one and different content is a rollback; when exactly one exists it is kept as last_previous and the others are deletable, as in 0.11.2; a generation that cannot be read completely holds every generation deletion; the reference file is not rewritten by such a deletion

findings.fix: the passage now points to the protection design and states the earlier-format rule and the release of legacy_untracked generations
